action_items: Alex Chen: Send draft POC statement of work and pricing (due 2025-12-06)
Priya Nair: Prepare benchmark plan and test harness (due 2025-12-08)

summary: AE + SE from Redwood ran a POC scoping call with StrataCore to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and integration options. Customer is evaluating OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs, and function/tool calling for a structured output pipeline. Key concerns: latency vs cost, data residency, SOC2/KMS, and timeline for a 4-week technical POC with benchmarks. Agreed to share SOW, security docs, and a benchmark plan.
topics: tool/function calling and structured JSON output
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-03 16:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood)  Maya Patel, Daniel Ruiz, Leah Gomez (StrataCore)

Summary (auto): short notes captured by recorder - high level alignment on POC scope, benchmarks, integration surface.

00:00 Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood Inference, i have Priya our solutions engineer with me, how's it going over there?
00:06 Maya: hey Alex, good thanks, uh excited to dig in, we've been looking at a couple of options, trying to nail down a POC to test latency and quality against our current pipeline.
00:12 Priya: great, quick intro from our side and then we wanted to walk through success criteria, expected workload, and the integration approaches  SDKs versus direct OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and the function/tool calling patterns for structured output.
00:22 Daniel: sounds good. For context, we're replacing part of our ingestion QA flow with an LLM step that normalizes and classifies free text into JSON schema, so structured output and reliability are critical.
00:30 Alex: perfect, that's helpful. What's your current traffic look like? qps, tokens per request, concurrency?
00:36 Maya: currently peak is around 12 qps for the QA flow, average request is 450 tokens in, 120 tokens out, concurrency spikes to ~40 during batch windows. We're planning for buffer up to 100 qps in the POC to see scaling behavior.
00:48 Priya: ok that bandwidth is helpful  so for sizing we would target a dedicated small pool for the POC or a reserved hosted configuration depending on perf needs. For latency targets, what are you aiming for?
00:56 Daniel: sub 250ms per token is ideal, end-to-end 2000ms median for a 120 output token scenario  but cost matters, so tradeoffs if we need quantized models or batching.
01:08 Leah: from security side, we need SOC 2, audit logs, KMS for keys, and a VPC/private deployment option if we progress past POC. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC.
01:18 Alex: full checklistable ask  we'll send SOC2 artifacts and the security questionnaire. Redwood Private supports VPC and customer KMS; we can note that in the SOW.
01:26 Maya: great. On the integration side, we're heavy in Python Node microservices. We prefer an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so minimal code changes, and SDKs would be fine. Also interested in function calling / tool calling to get structured json back rather than parsing free text.
01:40 Priya: yes our platform supports OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and SDKs in python/node/java. Function calling is supported  you can register a schema and we can return structured JSON, or stream tokens if you need streaming for UX. Note: streaming with structured output may need careful handling in client.
01:55 Daniel: quick question  do you support tool calling, like invoking our internal enrichment services (synonymizer, lookup) via the runtime?
02:02 Priya: we have a pattern for tool integrations  the model can emit a call and the agent framework can invoke a webhook to your service. For POC we usually mock the external tool or run a small adapter service. There can be latency added so we typically keep tool calls async or batched.
02:16 Maya: ok, that's fine. For success criteria, here's what we're thinking: 1) structured output accuracy >= 92% on our gold set; 2) median end-to-end latency <= 2s at 12 qps; 3) acceptable cost per 1k requests (TBD); and 4) no data persistence on shared infra (we need data retention controls).
02:34 Alex: that sounds concrete  we'll map those into measurable benchmarks. For benchmarking, can you share a sample of the dataset and a set of evaluation prompts?
02:41 Maya: yes, we'll share a redacted sample and the gold labels after the call. Expect ~5k examples for the POC bench.
02:48 Priya: perfect. For the benchmark harness we suggest: 1) offline accuracy eval on gold set; 2) load test for concurrency to validate latency SLOs; 3) an A/B compare vs your current infra to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
02:59 Daniel: how do model variants and quantization play in here? we want lowest cost but don't want to sacrifice accuracy.
03:06 Priya: we recommend starting with a 7B or 13B open model variant we host with int8 quantization for cost, then run a quality regression test. If accuracy drops below your threshold we'll fallback to a float16 variant on more capable hardware. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload.
03:24 Leah: about audit logs and key management  does Redwood expose per-request logs and is that compatible with our SIEM?
03:29 Alex: yes we expose request/response metadata (token counts, latency, route) and can integrate logs with your SIEM via secure export; payloads containing sensitive data can be excluded. KMS integrations supported for Private.
03:40 Maya: timeline  we want a 3-4 week POC: week 0 on-boarding and dataset prep, week 1 baseline offline eval, week 2 load/latency benchmarks, week 3 iterate on prompts/variants and handover. Is that realistic?
03:51 Priya: totally realistic. We'll scope the SOW for a 4-week engagement and include bench plan. We'll need staging keys and optional temporary private deployment for full routing test.
03:59 Daniel: for integrations, how invasive is the SDK change? we want to keep minimal footprint  ideally swap endpoints and define a small adapter for function calls.
04:07 Priya: with the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you mostly change the base URL and the client config. For function calling you define the JSON schema and the SDK will surface the function call object. We can provide client examples in python/node and a small sample adapter.
04:19 Alex: also note rate limiting and quotas  we'll recommend token-level limits and suggest burst capacity for your batch windows. For the POC we can enable a burst policy.
04:27 Maya: how do you measure cost during the POC? we want transparency on token cost and inference VM cost.
04:32 Alex: console will show per-route token and latency breakdowns, plus an estimated cost report. For Dedicated or Private we'll provide expected unit cost projections.
04:39 Daniel: any limitations on structured streaming? sometimes our UI consumes partial JSON while streaming to show progressive results.
04:45 Priya: streaming structured JSON can be done, but it requires the client to assemble and validate chunks; we recommend delimiting tokens or using a streaming json wrapper. We'll include a sample stream client for that.
04:56 Leah: on compliance we need data residency controls  can we pin region and ensure logs stay in region?
05:02 Alex: yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated/Private; hosted has region options in our cloud regions list, but Dedicated gives you stronger guarantees. We'll note that as a progression post-POC if residency is required.
05:11 Maya: ok good. One more: do you support model rollouts / canary testing? we want to test a small percentage against Redwood while keeping majority on current infra.
05:18 Priya: yes, rollout controls are built-in  canary, A/B, auto fallback on regressions. We'll help configure the routing rules for the POC.
05:26 Daniel: sample artifacts  can you send the SDK snippets and a sample function-calling schema?
05:30 Alex: yes, we'll attach code snippets, a small repo with adapter examples, and a starter function schema.
05:35 Maya: ok thanks  on acceptance criteria we also want defined metrics for quality drift and alerts if regression exceeds 2 points.
05:42 Priya: we can wire quality monitoring into Redwood Optimize alerts tied to your eval set; we'll include that in the SOW options.
05:49 (crosstalk) Leah: also need to confirm the NDA and who signs  our legal is cc'd  
05:53 Alex: we'll send the NDA and link the security questionnaire.
05:56 Priya: quick note on bench reproducibility  please include random seed and prompt templates so we can replicate results.
06:02 Maya: yes will do.
06:05 Alex: high-level recap  we have success criteria: >=92% structured accuracy, median latency <=2s at 12 qps, cost targets TBD; POC 3-4 weeks with dataset ~5k examples; integration via OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs; function calling for structured JSON; security: SOC2, KMS, SSO; action items and we agreed to share SOW, security docs, and bench plan.
06:25 Daniel: perfect, what's next week look like for kickoff?
06:29 Alex: we'll circulate the SOW and NDA by EOD tomorrow. Priya will follow up with the benchmark plan and a sample repo. If you can share the dataset by Friday we'll schedule bench runs the following week.
06:41 Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
06:44 Leah: thanks all.
06:46 Alex: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts  speaker labels may be off by one line in spots; some technical terms transcribed fuzzily (KV cache -> K V cash, quant -> quan.)

Attachments mentioned: SOW draft link (sent after call), security questionnaire link, sample repo with SDK snippets and function-calling examples, benchmark plan spreadsheet.
